title: Parametric universal arrows on the domain of a partial adjoint
statement:
Use the universe and quasicategory conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and coherent functors, transformations and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of quasicategories fitting in a fixed universe, and let $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$ be a full subcategory. Suppose that for each $d\in\mathcal D_0$ there exist $r_d\in\mathcal C$ and $\epsilon_d:T(r_d)\to d$ such that for every $c\in\mathcal C$ the map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,r_d)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(T(c),d),\qquad u\longmapsto\epsilon_d\circ T(u),$$
is an equivalence. Then there exist a coherent functor $R:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal C$ and a coherent transformation $\epsilon:TR\to\iota$, where $\iota:\mathcal D_0\hookrightarrow\mathcal D$, whose component at each $d$ is a universal arrow of the displayed kind. The space of these universal-arrow choices, including $R$ and $\epsilon$, is contractible. No assertion that $TR(d)$ lies in $\mathcal D_0$ is imposed.

For every simplicial set $K$ in this universe and coherent diagrams $A:K\to\mathcal C$, $B:K\to\mathcal D_0$, postcomposition with this transformation gives a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(A,RB)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)}(TA,\iota B),\qquad u\longmapsto(\epsilon B)\circ T(u).$$
It is compatible with evaluation at every vertex of $K$ and with precomposition by simplicial maps $K'\to K$. The assertions include their opposites: universal arrows $d\to T(l_d)$ assemble to a partial left adjoint with the dual coherent-diagram mapping-space formula. Universes can be enlarged throughout; $K$ need not be small in a previously fixed smaller universe.

source.place: Agent-formulated parametric version of the universal-arrow/representable-profunctor criterion: Proposition 8.3.4.1 and Remark 8.3.4.7, with the local adjoint criterion of Subsection 6.2.6 and its dual. The coherent-diagram clause is required explicitly; the cited local criterion by itself is not an attribution of that entire clause. WANTED: archived proof of this partial parametric form. No matching Stacks tag.

proof.text:
Work in a universe containing all the simplicial sets in question. Form the coherent comma quasicategory
$$E=\mathcal C\times_{\mathcal D,\mathrm{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal D)\times_{\mathrm{ev}_1,\mathcal D}\mathcal D_0.$$
Write its objects as $e=(c,d,a:Tc\to\iota d)$ and its target projection as $p:E\to\mathcal D_0$. Here and below the same construction may be made for any two functors into a quasicategory. Endpoint restriction is an isofibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], applied to $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and $\mathcal D\to *$. Its pullback gives $E$ as a quasicategory by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit]. The projection $p$ is an isofibration: the pullback endpoint map is one, and the projection $\mathcal C\times\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal D_0$ fills inner horns using those of $\mathcal C$ and lifts an equivalence with the identity of its $\mathcal C$-coordinate.
For $e'=(c',d',a')$, the mapping-space calculation is
$$\operatorname{Map}_E(e,e')\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,c')\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Tc,\iota d')}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D_0}(d,d'),\tag{*}$$
with legs $h\mapsto a'Th$ and $b\mapsto\iota(b)a$. To justify (*) rather than assume a comma theorem: in the arrow mapping-space model $U$, maps in this degreewise pullback are the pullback of $U_{\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal D)}(a,a')$ along $U_{\mathcal C}(c,c')\times U_{\mathcal D_0}(d,d')$. The endpoint map on these $U$ spaces is a Kan fibration by the last clause of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Thus this strict pullback computes the homotopy pullback by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Use the endpoint-compatible square formula [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square], the natural pinch equivalences [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], and homotopy-pullback invariance [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to obtain (*). Its projection to the second factor is the actual functor $p$ on mapping spaces. All comparisons preserve the specified endpoint projections and coherent composition. Explicitly, after the endpoint base change the path-space model consists of triples $(h,b,\gamma)$ with $\gamma:a'Th\simeq\iota(b)a$, which is exactly the right side of (*). If an endpoint comparison commutes only by its specified homotopy, insert that homotopy before or after $\gamma$; the inverse comparison inserts the reverse homotopy. Path concatenation and cancellation give inverse homotopies. Thus the use of homotopy-pullback invariance does not assume that a merely homotopy-commutative square commutes strictly.

source.place: Agent proof for paragraph 2: comma construction and its mapping-space formula from the existing endpoint theorems

proof.text:
Let $U\subset E$ be the full subcategory of universal arrows, namely those $(r,d,\epsilon)$ for which $h\mapsto\epsilon Th$ is an equivalence for every $c\in\mathcal C$. This is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. If the target $u=(r,d',\epsilon)$ is in $U$, the first leg of (*) is an equivalence, even when its source $e=(c,d,a)$ is an arbitrary object of $E$. Its pullback therefore makes
$$p_*:\operatorname{Map}_E(e,u)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D_0}(d,d')$$
an equivalence; this is the pullback of an equivalence of spaces, justified by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. In particular $p_U=p|_U$ is fully faithful. It hits every object of $\mathcal D_0$ by the hypothesis of the item. Its full essential image is therefore all of $\mathcal D_0$, so [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] supplies a coherent inverse $s:\mathcal D_0\to U$ and a specified equivalence $\beta:p_Us\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Project $s$ to $\mathcal C$ to get $R$. The arrows of $s$, followed by $\iota\beta$, give $\epsilon:TR\to\iota$. Composing a universal arrow with an equivalence of targets preserves its mapping-space universal property. This constructs the requested partial adjoint without requiring that $TR(d)$ land in $\mathcal D_0$.

source.place: Agent proof for paragraph 2: full universal-arrow subcategory is equivalent to the partial domain

proof.text: The choice space is the space of sections of $p_U$, or equivalently its homotopy-section space consisting of $(s,\beta:p_Us\simeq\mathrm{id})$. These include the representing arrows, hence precisely the data $(R,\epsilon)$ in the assertion, with their higher coherences. We verify the equivalence of these models. Universality is invariant under equivalences in $E$: the two endpoint components are equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], and conjugating (*) by their inverse edges preserves its universal maps. Thus $U$ is replete in $E$. The isofibration $p$ of Step 1 lifts equivalences to objects still in $U$, so $p_U$ is an isofibration. [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] makes $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal D_0,p_U)$ an isofibration. Its strict fiber at the identity computes the homotopy fiber on cores by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit]. Postcomposition with $p_U$ is an equivalence of functor quasicategories: whisker the inverse $s$ and the two coherent inverse equivalences of Step 2. Whiskering is the simplicial exponential operation, and the resulting transformations are equivalences by the componentwise criterion [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Hence the map on cores is an equivalence. Its homotopy fiber at the identity is contractible: transport along an inverse identifies it with pairs $(x,\gamma:x\simeq x_0)$, which contract to $(x_0,\mathrm{id})$ by their specified paths. The core of the strict section fiber is therefore contractible as well. This establishes the choice-space assertion; it is not a claim that the space of representing objects with their arrows forgotten is contractible.

source.place: Agent proof for paragraph 2: contractibility of the complete representing data, via sections of an equivalence

proof.text: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow E$. For each $e=(c,d,a)$ choose a universal $u_d=(r_d,d,\epsilon_d)$. The homotopy fiber over $a$ of the universal equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,r_d)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Tc,d)$ is contractible and nonempty. A point of it is a morphism $v_e:e\to j(u_d)$ together with a specified path $p(v_e)\simeq\mathrm{id}_d$, by the projection-compatible formula (*). For any $u\in U$, both $\operatorname{Map}_U(u_d,u)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D_0}(d,p_Uu)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_E(e,ju)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D_0}(d,p_Uu)$ are equivalences by Step 2. Precomposition with $v_e$ commutes with these projections up to the specified path $p(v_e)\simeq\mathrm{id}_d$, so it too is an equivalence. These are precisely the objectwise hypotheses of [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] for the functor $j$. It gives $L:E\to U$, a coherent unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}_E\to jL$, a counit, and coherent triangle identities. Moreover $p\eta:p\to p_UL$ is a natural equivalence. Indeed at $e$ both $v_e$ and $\eta_e$ are universal arrows into $j$; their universal equivalences produce mutually inverse comparison maps between their targets (each composite represents the original arrow). Thus $\eta_e$ is $v_e$ followed by $j$ of an equivalence. Its image under $p$ is an equivalence, and the componentwise criterion [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] proves the claim about $p\eta$.

source.place: Agent proof for paragraph 2: auxiliary reflection of arbitrary comma arrows into universal arrows

proof.text:
Fix any simplicial set $K$, enlarging the universe to make it small. All functor simplicial sets used here are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Whisker the adjunction $L\dashv j$ of Step 4 by $K$. This gives the equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(a,jV)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,U)}(La,V).$$
Here the forward map is $k\mapsto\delta_V\circ Lk$, with $\delta$ the counit; its inverse is $h\mapsto jh\circ\eta_a$. Naturality and the two triangle identities from [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] make these composites homotopic to the identity on the entire mapping spaces, including higher simplices. These are the same formulas applied to maps $K\times\Delta^n$, so they hold for arbitrary simplicial $K$, not just nerves. Also $\operatorname{Fun}(K,p_U)$ is an equivalence by whiskering its inverse as in Step 3, and thus induces equivalences on mapping spaces by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Combining the two gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(a,jsB)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D_0)}(p_ULa,p_UsB).$$
Precompose with the equivalence $p\eta_a:pa\simeq p_ULa$ and postcompose with $\beta B:p_UsB\simeq B$. Naturality of $\eta$ and the adjunction triangle identify the resulting map with $k\mapsto\beta B\circ p(k)$. Thus this actual target-projection map is an equivalence to $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D_0)}(pa,B)$. Composition by the specified equivalences is invertible on mapping spaces using their inverse transformations and their inverse homotopies.

source.place: Agent proof for paragraph 2: whiskered reflection; explicit inverse formulas instead of assuming a pointwise mapping theorem

proof.text:
Now fix $A:K\to\mathcal C$, $B:K\to\mathcal D_0$, and a transformation $\alpha:TA\to\iota B$. It is exactly a diagram $a=(A,B,\alpha):K\to E$. Degreewise exponential identities identify $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ with the comma construction for $T_*:\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)$ and $\iota_*:\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D_0)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)$: reorder $K\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ and take degreewise pullbacks. Thus the calculation (*) from Step 1 applies to these functor quasicategories as well. It identifies the homotopy fiber over $\mathrm{id}_B$ of the target-projection map in Step 5 with the homotopy fiber over $\alpha$ of
$$\Phi_{A,B}:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(A,RB)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)}(TA,\iota B),\qquad h\longmapsto(\epsilon B)\circ T(h).$$
The comparison $\beta B$ in Step 5 is exactly the one used to define $\epsilon$, so this is the displayed map in the item. Step 5 makes every such fiber contractible. The source and target of $\Phi_{A,B}$ are Kan complexes by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] now makes $\Phi_{A,B}$ an equivalence; if its target is empty, its source must be empty and the same criterion still applies. All constructions are functors, endpoint restriction, coherent composition and the same whiskered unit/counit, so restricting $K$ to any vertex or along any simplicial map $K'\to K$ commutes with the map $\Phi$ and its coherence homotopies. This proves naturality and both parameter compatibilities. Reversing simplex order gives the dual argument for $T^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $\mathcal D_0^{\mathrm{op}}$ still full. The opposite mapping-space homotopy types are identified by the natural pinch equivalences [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] and reversal of the arrow interval; reversal of realization coordinates identifies the opposite Kan complex with the same homotopy type. Taking parameter $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ gives the partial left adjoint and the dual formula. No presentability, global completeness, or smaller-universe bound was used.

Updated source attribution, title, searches and report consistently. No new nodes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NC-82375baf7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all six steps, the statements of the ten cited nodes, the two definition dependencies, the unit record, the blueprint place (main-20261015 prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint proof, paragraph 2) and the three citers. The restored statement is the true partial right adjoint (universal arrow) theorem for quasicategories, and the citers use exactly these clauses. Edge cases checked: TR(d) outside D_0 in the poset x<d; empty K; empty D_0; a groupoid case showing that epsilon must stay in the choice space. Step checks: (1) the comma E is a pullback of the exponentiation corner isofibration, and (*) follows from the Kan-fibration clause, right properness, arrow-square and pinch, with homotopy insertion written out. (2) A universal target makes the first leg of (*) an equivalence, so p_U is fully faithful; the hypothesis gives surjectivity, and full-essential-image gives s and beta. (3) U is replete, so p_U is an isofibration; the section fiber of Fun(D_0,U) is exactly the (R,epsilon) data, and its core is the homotopy fiber of an equivalence, hence contractible. (4) The local adjoint criterion applied to j: U to E has exactly its objectwise hypotheses verified, and p(eta) is an equivalence. (5) The whiskered L, j and the explicit target-projection map check. (6) The comma identification of Fun(K,E), the fiber match with Phi using the same beta, the fiber criterion, restriction naturality, and the dual via reversing Delta^1 all check. No new nodes. Not duplicates: lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion and lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion are total and non-parametric.
